Every Make.com scenario fails eventually: an AI module times out or an API hits a rate limit. With no error handler, that lead just stops mid-run.

Here's a beginner setup that catches failures and retries them automatically 🧵

First, the setting that's easy to miss: Scenario settings (gear icon, bottom toolbar) → 'Allow storing of incomplete executions'. Break can't save failed bundles without it. Leave 'Enable data loss' off.

Next: right-click the AI module → Add error handler. On the new route:
1. Email yourself the error type, message and lead details
2. End with Break: automatic completion on, ~3 attempts, 15–30 min apart so rate limits can reset

The 5 handlers, one line each:
Break: save the bundle, retry later
Resume: carry on with a fallback value
Ignore: drop it (only for steps you can lose)
Commit/Rollback: database transactions only. They can't unsend an email.

Rule of thumb: retry only temporary errors (timeouts, rate limits, connection problems). Bad credentials or bad data will fail every time, and retries use operations. Send those to an alert and fix them yourself.

Last tip: test it before a real failure. Clone the scenario, give it its own webhook, break the AI module on purpose, send a fake lead. Check for the alert, a History warning and the Incomplete executions entry. Full guide: {URL}

reddit_title: Make.com error handling for beginners: which of the 5 handlers to use, plus a retry setup for AI timeouts and rate limits
reddit_post:
**TL;DR:** Turn on "Allow storing of incomplete executions" in Scenario settings. Then right-click any fragile module (especially AI modules), add an error handler, send yourself an email alert, and end the route with **Break**, set to retry about 3 times, 15–30 minutes apart. Save the other handlers for specific cases.

---

**What happens if you don't add an error handler?**

The run stops at the failing module and is marked as an error. Nothing after that module runs for that bundle. If errors keep happening, Make can deactivate the scenario. If incomplete executions are enabled, Make may store the failed run, and its docs describe automatic retries for some temporary error types. Still, it's safer to add your own handlers to important modules.

**The 5 handlers in plain English**

- **Break:** stores the failed bundle as an incomplete execution and can retry it automatically. This is the best default for AI timeouts and rate limits.
- **Resume:** treats the module as if it succeeded, using substitute output you define, so the modules after it still run with your fallback values. Use it when a placeholder is better than stopping.
- **Ignore:** drops the failed bundle and moves on. Nothing after that module happens for that item. Only use it for steps you can truly afford to lose.
- **Commit / Rollback:** for database transactions. They only affect modules that support transactions. They can't unsend an email or delete a CRM record.

**Setup, step by step**

1. Open the scenario, click the settings (gear) icon in the bottom toolbar, and switch on **Allow storing of incomplete executions**. Break needs this.
2. In the same panel, leave **Enable data loss** off. Decide whether you really need **Sequential processing**, because when it's on, stored failures can hold back later runs. Note the **Number of consecutive errors** limit, then save.
3. Right-click the AI module (OpenAI, Anthropic, etc.) and choose **Add error handler**. This creates a route that only runs when that module fails.
4. Make the first module on that route an Email/Gmail "Send an email" to yourself. Map in the error type and message, the lead's name and email from the trigger, and the scenario name, so you can act without opening Make.
5. End the route with **Break**. Turn on automatic completion and set about 3 attempts with a 15–30 minute interval, so a rate limit has time to reset.
6. *Optional:* add a router after the email. Filter one path to temporary errors (e.g. ConnectionError, RateLimitError, ModuleTimeoutError) and end it in Break with retries on. End the other path in Break with retries off, so permanent errors wait for you to fix them. Check the current error type names in Make's docs.
7. **Test on a clone.** Clone the scenario, give the clone its own new webhook, and leave it switched off. Make its AI module fail on purpose, for example by mapping a field you leave blank into the required prompt field. Click "Run once", then send a fake lead to the clone's webhook.
8. **Verify:** the alert email arrived, History shows a warning, and the bundle is listed in Incomplete executions. Fix the cause and retry the bundle once to prove retries work. Then delete the test data and switch on the original scenario.

**Things that trip people up**

- **Only retry temporary errors.** Bad credentials or bad data will never succeed on retry. Each automatic retry runs the scenario again from the failed module and uses operations (or credits, depending on your plan).
- **Error routes cost operations too.** Modules on an error route count like any other module, so keep an eye on usage in your dashboard.
- **Manual retries:** go to the scenario's Incomplete executions tab, fix the underlying problem first, then retry one item or select several. Make continues from the module that failed.
- **Coming from Zapier?** Autoreplay overlaps with Break, but it's a single setting and Zapier controls the retry schedule. Break lets you set the number of attempts and the interval for each module, and you can combine it with alerts and error-type filters.

Make renames menu labels from time to time, so if something doesn't match what you see, check the Make Help Center.

---

*Disclosure: I wrote a longer version of this guide with an FAQ: {URL}. Everything above should be enough to set it up without clicking through.*
